conviction_note: No usable option chain and no single decisive unpriced number: the largest item (the 3 Sep restructuring 8-K, $40-45M Q3 charge for a $37-42M annual PPNR uplift, ~10% of annual EPS) is public and left the stock unmoved, and the call is where it turns into a 2027 frame; the Fed's 16 Sep hike against a guide that assumed two cuts helps an asset-sensitive book, while rising FHLB reliance, a $44M nonaccrual construction credit and a revenue consensus that looks ~1-2% rich against Q2's run rate pull the other way. Findings sum +0.40, the scaled number is +0.18 (p_up 53 x abs 3.0); both small, same sign, no tension to resolve.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS consensus $0.53: Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/sfnc/earnings-forecasts and AlphaQuery https://www.alphaquery.com/stock/SFNC/earnings-history agree at $0.53; AAII (2026-10-15) gives $0.53 from 7 analysts for the quarter, with 2 down / 1 up revisions in the last month https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/515594-what-you-need-to-know-about-simmons-first-national-corporations-q3-earnings. Revenue consensus $253.8M (Benzinga) to ~$255-257M (TickFlow/aggregators). Company guide: FY2026 NII +9-11% (management 'very comfortable' with top end on the Q2 call), noninterest expense growth below the prior 2-3%, NCOs <25bp, double-digit PPNR growth. My read: adjusted EPS ~$0.53-0.55 (+1% on EPS), revenue ~$250-253M (~-1% vs revenue consensus). GAAP EPS will carry the pre-announced $40-45M pre-tax restructuring charge (~$0.22-0.24/share after tax), so GAAP prints ~$0.30.
positioning_check: Short interest ~5.8M shares, ~4.0% of float, ~3.0 days to cover (Equibles, ~2026-08-19 settlement, https://equibles.com/stocks/SFNC); FINRA 2026-06-30 5.1M / 2.8 days (CurvedTrading https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/sfnc/). Not crowded. No skew: the front-month chain is unusable (4 contracts of open interest, ATM legs not two-sided), so the market makes no directional statement through options. Tape: -2.4% over 20 days, -0.22% over 5, 7.4% under the 52-week high; down ~4% since the Q2 print vs SPY +2.6% (AAII). Stock closed $22.98 on the day of the restructuring 8-K (2026-09-03, talkbusiness) and sits at $22.33 now, i.e. the PPNR plan bought nothing.

findings.finding: 8-K filed 2026-09-03 (Items 2.05 and 7.01): SFNC will close 26 branches on 2026-12-04 and run broader operating-model initiatives, booking substantially all of $40-45M pre-tax charges in Q3 2026 (branches $20-23M, mostly non-cash real-estate write-downs; only $4-5M cash) for a $37-42M annual PPNR uplift once fully implemented, with some possibly reinvested; no timeline and no 2026 guide update. At ~21% tax and 145M diluted shares the uplift is ~$0.20-0.23/share a year against a ~$2.05 trailing EPS (~10%), and the Q3 call (16 Oct) is the first place management can say when it lands and how much is reinvested, i.e. a 2027 frame. The stock closed $22.98 on 3 Sep and is $22.33 today, so the market has paid nothing for it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has been what moves SFNC: the Q4 2025 print (2026-01-20), which came with the 2026 outlook (NII +9-11%, double-digit PPNR), rose +8.92%; Q1 2026 +5.18%; the Q2 2026 miss with no guide change -1.29% (baseline). Downside path: a GAAP headline near $0.30 vs $0.53 and a large reinvestment share would dilute the story.
findings.why_not_priced: If priced, the stock would have re-rated on 3-4 Sep and Q4/2027 EPS revisions would be up; instead it is 2.8% below the 3 Sep close and AAII shows net negative revisions (2 down, 1 up) over the last month. Without a timeline or a reinvestment number, sell-side cannot model it, so the call supplies the missing piece.
findings.independence: Same document as the GAAP-charge observation (merged here, not filed twice). Press confirmation of figures: https://talkbusiness.net/2026/09/simmons-first-to-close-26-branches-including-six-in-arkansas/ (same underlying 8-K, not independent).

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0), after holding at 3.50-3.75% all year, while SFNC's January 2026 margin outlook assumed cuts in May and August; SFNC describes itself as slightly asset sensitive (NII +1.51% to +3.02% for +100/+200bp per its Q2 disclosure), so the rate path is running ahead of the company's own guide assumptions, supporting the top end of FY NII +9-11% and a firmer Q4/2027 margin talk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII/NIM outlook has been the stock's main line since the 2025 repositioning: +8.92% on the print that delivered the 3.81% Q4 NIM and the 2026 NII guide; -1.29% when NIM stalled at 3.84% in Q2 with an EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro is public, so part is priced; what is not is the company-specific translation: sell-side consensus revenue moved little (revisions slightly negative), and only management can say how much of the hike passes through given its shift toward short-term FHLB funding. Macro-to-company transmission, unconfirmed by the company, hence small.
findings.independence: Company rate-sensitivity and guide assumptions: https://quartr.com/events/simmons-first-national-corporation-sfnc-q2-2026_ozDNfe8I and the Q4 2025 call recap (cuts in May and August assumed) https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/simmons-first-national-q4-earnings-call-highlights-2026-01-21/. Proxy, not company-confirmed for Q3.

findings.finding: Arkansas peer Home BancShares (reported 2026-10-14): Q3 NIM 4.53% vs 4.51%, interest-bearing deposit cost down to 2.37% from 2.39%, zero provision, NCOs $2.1M; but loans fell $217M and NPLs rose to $200.8M from $185.3M, mostly Texas. The closest same-footprint read says deposit pricing in Arkansas/Texas did not get worse in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No attributed SFNC reaction to a peer print; SFNC's own deposit-cost line was flat-to-down in Q1-Q2 2026 (1.96% to 1.93%).
findings.why_not_priced: Landed yesterday after the close, after SFNC's consensus was set (no estimate change visible since); a single peer print rarely moves another name's estimates the day before its own release.
findings.independence: Proxy. Points against it: FB Financial (next finding) and First Horizon's flat-to-down NIM (3.48% vs 3.49%) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000178/a3q26earningsslides-fina.htm.

findings.finding: Tennessee peer FB Financial (reported 2026-10-13): Q3 NIM fell 12bp to 3.83%, with interest-bearing deposit cost up to 2.88% from 2.81% and total deposit cost up to 2.32% from 2.26%, attributed to higher funding costs; adjusted fees fell and mortgage income dropped. SFNC has Tennessee exposure and the same funding-cost risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SFNC fell -1.29% on Q2 when NIM stopped expanding and EPS missed.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer print two days ago; SFNC estimates have not visibly moved since. Part of FBK's compression was its own deposit growth push, which SFNC is not pursuing (SFNC deposits fell in H1).
findings.independence: Proxy. HOMB points the other way (finding above), so the two peer reads largely offset.

findings.finding: SFNC's own funding mix worsened through H1: total deposits fell $456M year-to-date to $19.73B (time deposits -$468M, brokered reduced) while other borrowings rose $639M to $941M, largely short-term FHLB advances, and the Fed then hiked on 16 Sep, so a growing slice of liabilities reprices immediately; management said deposits are 'one of our biggest focuses' with likely significant investment over 12-24 months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (deposits down $0.5B, borrowings up, NIM flat at 3.84%) traded -1.29%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sits in the 10-Q balance sheet and cash-flow statement, not in the headline release metrics wire copy carries (NIM, EPS); the interaction with a September hike that the guide did not assume has not been written up anywhere found. If priced, revenue consensus would sit nearer Q2's $248.5M run rate than $254-257M.
findings.independence: Q2 release figures (deposits $19.7B vs $20.2B, other borrowings $941M vs $447M) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000090498/000119312526306164/d123214dex991.htm, same company, different document. Partly offsets the rate finding above; they are the two halves of asset sensitivity and are kept apart because one is a macro proxy and the other a company number.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 noninterest income of $47.9M (up from $44.2M) was lifted by swap fee income and a positive SBIC valuation adjustment, while revenue consensus for Q3 is $253.8-257M against Q2's adjusted $248.5M (NII $200.6M + fees $47.9M); hitting it needs roughly +$5-9M sequentially, which a ~$3-4M NII step plus flat-or-lower fees does not deliver, so a ~1-2% revenue shortfall is the likely print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue $251.6M vs $256.3M consensus with EPS $0.50 vs $0.53: -1.29% (Chartmill/search summary; baseline move).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue sits above the Q2 run rate even after Q2 missed revenue by ~$5M; aggregators do not strip SBIC marks. EPS can still meet the bar via a lower provision (Q2 provision $17.4M exceeded NCOs by $8.3M), so this is a quality-of-print item rather than an EPS miss.
findings.independence: Consensus figures: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/sfnc/earnings-forecasts. My arithmetic, an inference from the company's numbers.

findings.finding: Credit: NPLs rose to $166.0M (0.92% of loans) from $141.9M in Q2, driven by a single 1-4 family construction relationship of ~$44.0M from the latest acquisition that fully migrated to nonaccrual; the CEO said resolution timing 'could extend into next year'. A charge-off or further migration in Q3 is the main downside path; guide is NCOs <25bp (Q2 0.20%). Peer HOMB showed rising Texas NPLs this quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (NPL jump on this credit first disclosed) +5.18% as the rest was clean; Q2 2026 (full migration, NPLs +$24M, provision build) -1.29%.
findings.why_not_priced: Known credit, so mostly priced; what is unpriced is the outcome, which is two-sided (a resolution or a reserve already held would be a relief). Sized as a small negative for the skew of outcomes, not a confirmed loss.
findings.independence: Q2 call commentary as summarised in search results; HOMB Texas NPLs up https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000133152026000117/homb093026earningsrelease.htm (proxy).

findings.finding: Loan repricing tailwind already disclosed: ~$1.8B of fixed-rate loans reprice over the next 12 months at an average yield below 4%, against a ready-to-close pipeline at 6.73% and Q2 committed production of $1.8B, the highest in almost four years; this is inside the FY NII +9-11% guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan growth and NII lines were the drivers of the +8.92% Q4 2025 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is in the company's own guide. Filed small because the pace of repricing in the first full quarter is unmodelled by outsiders.
findings.independence: Same release as the fee finding; distinct line.

findings.finding: Expense: on the Q2 call management said it expects to beat its 2-3% FY noninterest expense growth outlook; adjusted noninterest expense was $140.3M in Q2 vs $140.6M in Q1, adjusted efficiency 54.26%. Inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Efficiency gains were part of the Q4 2025/Q1 2026 positive reactions; no isolated read.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced (company said it); kept small.
findings.independence: Call recap (search summary of nasdaq/marketbeat call highlights): https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/simmons-first-national-q2-earnings-call-highlights

findings.finding: Capital return: SFNC bought back 662,082 shares in Q2 at an average $21.52 with ~$161M left on the 2026 authorization (CET1 11.60%), and the stock has traded around $22-23 through Q3, so continued repurchase likely trimmed the share count.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and partly in estimates; filed for completeness.

findings.finding: Positioning: the bar has been drifting down into the print (AAII: 2 downgrades vs 1 upgrade of estimates in the last month, revisions score 'Negative' 37; consensus $0.53 from 7) and the stock is -4.0% since the Q2 report vs SPY +2.6%, with short interest a modest ~4% of float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q3 2025 underperformance into print the stock rose +1.5%; no clean pattern.
findings.why_not_priced: A lowered bar is by definition visible; small.

outside_window.finding: Branch closures take effect 2026-12-04; the PPNR benefit begins accruing only after that and is realised through 2027, so the realised savings cannot be seen inside this window (only management's framing of them on the 16 Oct call, filed above).

lessons_applied: Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission unconfirmed by the company): Fed-hike finding cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
